chunks: The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me of it, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said:

Sulayman ibn Rushayd wrote to him, informing him that he had urinated in the darkness of the night, and that his palm was touched by the coolness of a drop of urine. He had no doubt that it had touched him, but he did not see it. He wiped it with a cloth, then forgot to wash it, and applied oil, rubbing with it his two palms, his face, and his head; then he performed wudu (ablution) for salat (prayer) and prayed.

So he replied to him with an answer that I read in his own handwriting: As for what you merely supposed regarding what touched your hand, it is nothing unless it is established with certainty. If you were certain of that, then it would indeed be incumbent upon you to repeat the salat (prayers) that you had performed with that very wudu (ablution), namely those of them whose time still remained; but whatever had passed beyond its time, there is no repetition required of you for it. This is because when a man's garment is najis, he only repeats the salat that is still within its time; but if he is junub or he prayed without wudu (ablution), then he must repeat the obligatory salat (prayers) that he missed, because the garment is unlike the body.
So act according to that, if Allah wills.

key_terms.الْبَوْلِ: urine, the source of the najasah discussed in the ruling
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification performed for salat (prayer)
key_terms.بِخِرْقَةٍ: with a cloth, by which the hand was wiped instead of washed
key_terms.بِدُهْنٍ: with oil, which was spread over the hands, face, and head
key_terms.جُنُبًا: in a state of janabah, requiring ghusl (ritual bath)
key_terms.ظُلْمَةِ: the darkness of the night in which the incident occurred
key_terms.نَجِسًا: ritually impure, describing the garment in the legal comparison

ai.seo_question: If someone later becomes certain that urine touched his hand before wudu (ablution), which prayers must he repeat?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out a legal ruling concerning uncertainty and certainty in najasah and their effect on salat (prayer). It distinguishes between impurity on clothing, for which only prayers still within their time are repeated, and invalid bodily states such as janabah or lack of wudu (ablution), for which missed obligatory prayers must be repeated.
